title: Syntomicity is preserved and detected by etale source covers
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. In this statement, a morphism $g:T\to B$ is called syntomic if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and for every $b\in B$ every local ring of its scheme-theoretic fibre $T_b=T\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(b)$ in the meaning of [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion]. (1) If $f$ is syntomic and $h:U\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], then $f\circ h$ is syntomic. (2) If $(h_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ is a set-indexed family of etale morphisms whose images cover the underlying set of $X$, and every $f\circ h_i$ is syntomic, then $f$ is syntomic. No quasi-compactness, separation, Noetherianity, or field-base hypothesis is imposed. The empty covering family is allowed when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 036S (lemma-syntomic-syntomic-local-source); etale maps are syntomic by morphisms.tex Tag 02GQ (lemma-etale-syntomic). The stated fibre criterion is morphisms.tex Tags 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic) and 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection).

proof.text: First handle flatness and local finite presentation. For (1), precomposition by the etale $h$ preserves both properties by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], applied separately with $P$ flat and locally of finite presentation. For (2), the last assertion of the same node applied to the jointly surjective family $(h_i)$ descends these two properties from the composites. Thus in each direction $f$ and every composite under consideration are flat and locally of finite presentation. It remains to check the local rings of their ordinary fibres.

source.place: Tag 036S (lemma-syntomic-syntomic-local-source); flatness and local-finite-presentation part, also the first paragraph of Tag 05B7 (lemma-syntomic-permanence).

proof.text: For each locally finitely presented map $g:T\to S$ just obtained and each $s\in S$, write $k=\kappa(s)$. Its fibre $T_s$ is covered by affine opens with finitely presented $k$-algebras: take affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset T$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ with $s\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, use [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], and pull back to $s$. The pulled-back open is $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_R k)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; its algebra is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. These opens cover since they are inverse images of a source cover. Their displayed finite presentations give finite type by forgetting the finite list of relations. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] every stalk of $T_s$ is the localization at a prime of one such finite type $k$-algebra, hence is essentially of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tags 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic) and 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres), fibre-local-ring setup; affine fibre charts and finite presentation by base change.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and put $k=\kappa(s)$. For (1), base change $h$ to $e:U_s\to X_s$ using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. For (2), [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] makes the maps $e_i:(U_i)_s\to X_s$ etale and jointly surjective. Here $U\times_X X_s\cong U_s$ (and likewise for $U_i$): the forward map sends $(u,(x,t))$ with $h(u)=x$ to $(u,t)$, and the inverse sends $(u,t)$ to $(u,(h(u),t))$; these are inverse by the fibre-product universal property. Write $e:Z\to X_s$ for any such map, $z\in Z$, $x=e(z)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. Step 2 gives local $k$-algebras essentially of finite type. The local map $A\to B$ is flat because $e$ is etale and therefore flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 05B7 (lemma-syntomic-permanence), reduction to a fibre over a field; morphisms.tex Tag 02GO and topologies.tex etale covering base change.

proof.text: The closed fibre of $A\to B$ is $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong\kappa(z)$. Indeed, choose affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $z$ for $e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] the two stalks are the corresponding prime localizations. If these are $\operatorname{Spec}E'\subseteq Z$ over $\operatorname{Spec}E\subseteq X_s$ and $\mathfrak p\subset E$ is the prime of $x$, the fibre $Z_x$ meets $\operatorname{Spec}E'$ in the open subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(E'\otimes_E\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-iso] to $E\to E'$: the stalk at $z$ of the fibre over $x$ is $B/\mathfrak m_A B$ (localizing the base ideal at $x$ replaces it by $\mathfrak m_A$). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], that stalk is the field $\kappa(z)$, a finite separable extension of $\kappa(x)$. All these maps preserve the original $k$-action, as their fractions send $a/b$ to its image divided by the image of $b$. This field is essentially of finite type over $k$: if $B=W^{-1}D$ with $D$ finite type, its quotient is $\overline W^{-1}(D/J)$ for the inverse image $J$ of $\mathfrak m_A B$, and $D/J$ is generated by the images of the generators of $D$. It is a regular local ring of dimension zero, so is a complete-intersection local $k$-algebra by taking itself as regular presentation ring and the empty regular sequence in [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-local-ci-source-fibre] to conclude $B$ is CI over $k$ if and only if $A$ is CI over $k$.

source.place: Tags 09Q7 (lemma-avramov) and 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), applied to the flat local map on the ordinary fibre; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL describes its closed fibre.

proof.text: In (1), every $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is CI by syntomicity of $f$, so step 4 gives that every $\mathcal O_{U_s,z}$ is CI. Together with step 1 this proves $f\circ h$ syntomic. In (2), for each $s$ and $x\in X_s$, joint surjectivity in step 3 supplies $i$ and $z\in(U_i)_s$ over $x$. Syntomicity of $f\circ h_i$ makes $B$ CI; step 4 makes $A$ CI. Step 1 supplies flatness and local finite presentation of $f$, giving exactly syntomicity as defined in the item. If a fibre is empty there is no local ring to test. If $X$ is empty, flatness and local finite presentation and the fibre condition are all vacuous, so the empty covering family causes no exception.

lean.statement: theorem syntomic_etale_source_locality {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : ((Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ f.HasCompleteIntersectionFibres) → ∀ (U : Scheme.{u}) (h : U ⟶ X), Etale h → Flat (h ≫ f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (h ≫ f) ∧ (h ≫ f).HasCompleteIntersectionFibres) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (h : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X), (∀ i : I, Etale (h i)) → (∀ x : X, ∃ (i : I) (z : U i), h i z = x) → (∀ i : I, Flat (h i ≫ f) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (h i ≫ f) ∧ (h i ≫ f).HasCompleteIntersectionFibres) → Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ f.HasCompleteIntersectionFibres)
